status_summary: The government expanded DOE's role in reactor demonstration and deployment rather than limiting it. On 2025-12-02 DOE selected the Tennessee Valley Authority and Holtec for up to 400 million dollars each in cost-shared funding under its Gen III+ small modular reactor program to build first-mover plants, and Executive Order 14301 (signed 2025-05-23) directed DOE to create a Reactor Pilot Program, under which DOE reported on 2026-07-06 that four privately developed reactors had reached DOE-authorized criticality (three in June 2026 and a fourth on the Saturday before the release), exceeding the goal of three by 2026-07-04; DOE's Nuclear Energy Launch Pad, reported 2026-03-06, builds on the pilot programs and extends support beyond initial authorization. DOE announced conditional HALEU fuel allocations on 2025-08-26, including for a pilot program reactor, and the Office of Nuclear Energy continues under the Under Secretary for Energy after the 2025-11-20 reorganization (per a law-firm summary of DOE's announcement and a trade press report). Congress's FY2026 appropriation (Public Law 119-74, 2026-01-23) provided 1.685 billion dollars for Nuclear Energy, above the 1.37 billion requested, and transferred 3.1 billion dollars of infrastructure law funds for up to two advanced small modular reactors, per CRS.

timeline.event: Executive Order 14301 signed, directing DOE to create a Reactor Pilot Program (published 2025-05-29).
DOE announced a second round of conditional HALEU allocations to three companies, including fuel for a pilot program reactor.

DOE released an updated organization chart realigning the Department; the Office of Nuclear Energy sits under the Under Secretary for Energy, per a law-firm summary and a trade press report; the office remains.

DOE selected the Tennessee Valley Authority and Holtec for up to 400 million dollars each in federal cost-shared funding under the Gen III+ small modular reactor program to deploy first-mover reactor plants, from a 900 million dollar solicitation issued in March 2025.

FY2026 Energy and Water appropriations enacted (P.L. 119-74); per CRS, Nuclear Energy received 1.685 billion dollars and 3.1 billion dollars of infrastructure law funds were transferred for small modular reactor demonstrations.

World Nuclear News reports that DOE has established the Nuclear Energy Launch Pad, building on the Reactor Pilot Program (11 projects) and the Fuel Line Pilot Program (9 projects) and extending support beyond initial authorization to testing and operation; DOE provides resources rather than funding. The announcement date itself is not stated.

A Nuclear News report of 2026-07-02 had counted three.

title: Limit DOE Nuclear Energy scope and start no new reactor demonstrations
uncertainties: The pilot reactors are developed by private companies under DOE authorization, and Executive Order 14301 does not describe DOE funding for them; on their own they could be read as regulatory facilitation, so the diverged call rests mainly on the Gen III+ SMR awards and the larger budget. The DOE release does not name the funding appropriation or the office running the program, though the program page sits under the Office of Nuclear Energy's web path (an inference). The text respects existing contractual obligations; the SMR solicitation was issued in March 2025, after the period began. The placement of the Office of Nuclear Energy under the Under Secretary for Energy is read from a law-firm summary and a trade press article (American Nuclear Society); the text of DOE's 2025-11-20 organization chart read did not show reporting lines. The DOE criticality release does not give a calendar date for the fourth reactor (it says early Saturday, before its 2026-07-06 dateline), and the page metadata shows an earlier publish time that conflicts with its content; the dateline is used. The FY2027 Nuclear Energy request was not checked.
